title and abstract.summary: The study analyzed historical museum records of 300 moth species in an isolated forest reserve in North-East Italy over an 80-year period to investigate whether extinction risk was related to body size or ecological specialization. It measured changes in the moth community's mean wingspan and functional dispersion (FDis) over time. The study evaluated whether body size or functional specialization of insect species are linked to a higher risk of extinction in an isolated conservation area by analyzing historic and recent samples from the coastal pinewood reserve Pineta san Vitale in North-East
